author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Springfield Public Schools reopened Monday after a cyberattack forced the district to shut down last week, New England Public Media reported through NHPR.

The disruption came only about a week after the new school year began. Superintendent Sonia Dinnall spoke to reporters as students returned, while officials continued investigating the incident and its effect on district systems.

The reopening also came amid rumors that schools were unsafe. NEPM reported that attendance at one school was better Monday than it had been before the cyber incident, according to comments from Boland Elementary School Principal Lisa Bakowski.

The district’s return to in-person classes marks a shift from emergency response to recovery, but the investigation remains active. The initial report did not identify the group responsible for the attack or provide a complete account of which systems were affected.
Families should rely on announcements from Springfield Public Schools for operational changes, technology updates and any further instructions connected to the incident.
dek: Springfield Public Schools reopened Monday after a cyberattack shut the district down during the first weeks of the school year.
headline: Springfield schools reopen as cyberattack investigation continues
sourceName: New England Public Media via NHPR
